summary: Introductory intake between Redwood CSM/AE/SE and Stonefield platform + security + product to scope a 6-week pilot. Main concerns: data residency, SSO/KMS integration, latency vs cost tradeoffs, and whether Dedicated or Private deployment is required. Agreed to run a benchmark week and share SOC2 docs. Action owners assigned.
topics: Deployment mode: hosted vs dedicated vs private
Performance benchmarks and KV/prefix caching expectations
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for taking the time today. quick roll call?
[00:08] Kevin (Stonefield): Kevin here, head of platform.
[00:11] Maya (Stonefield SRE): Maya here.
[00:13] Liam (Stonefield CTO): Liam dialed in.
[00:15] Ava (Stonefield Security): Ava here from security.
[00:18] Jordan: perfect. Samira and Ethan from our side?
[00:20] Samira (Redwood CSM): yep, hi all. Samira here.
[00:22] Ethan (Redwood SE): Ethan on the SE side, will take point on the bench and network stuff.
[00:25] Jordan: awesome. objective — align on pilot success criteria, understand your stack constraints, and identify blockers for on-prem or VPC peering. quick background on Stonefield's use case?
[00:34] Rosa (Product): we want to embed an LLM assistant in our TMS dashboard to do manifest summarization, reranking candidate suggestions, and a support triage bot. must be below 300ms p95 for short prompts and retention rules for driver PII are strict.
[00:49] Jordan: good callout on latency and PII. are you planning to keep any requests or transcripts?
[00:55] Liam: no long-term storage of raw transcripts, we'll persist only structured metadata. retention window is 30 days for logs, but customer sensitive fields are redacted before we persist.
[01:06] Jordan: ok noted. Ava, from security perspective what are the must-haves?
[01:11] Ava: SOC2 is table stakes, we need KMS integration or HSM for at-rest keys, audit logs to show who called what model, and SSO - that's SAML with SCIM provisioning ideally. also network egress controls; we cannot send certain buckets to public endpoints.
[01:26] Samira: Redwood supports customer-managed KMS via our Private offering and we can integrate with most KMS providers. SSO via SAML + SCIM available on enterprise tier.
[01:35] Kevin: when you say private, do you mean fully air-gapped on prem, or VPC-hosted private control plane?
[01:41] Ethan: good distinction — we have two patterns: Redwood Private (VPC connector + private control plane) and an on-prem package for air-gapped. most customers do VPC peering or Private with customer-managed keys.
[01:52] Kevin: ok, our preference would be VPC peering first; on-prem would be heavier.
[01:58] Jordan: understood. timeline for pilot?
[02:00] Rosa: we'd like to have a working pilot in 6 weeks, with a production readiness decision at 12 weeks.
[02:06] Jordan: that's reasonable. bench and metrics we should capture?
[02:09] Ethan: we'll run a benchmark that mirrors live seq lengths. we'll look at p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, and cost per 1K tokens. also KV cache hit rates for prefix caching since that impacts cost and latency.
[02:22] Maya: a question — we have mostly 16K context prompts for manifests and some long queries, does Redwood support long-context models and is quantization going to hurt quality for us?
[02:32] Ethan: yes, runtime supports long-context models. quantization is model-dependent; for many of the curated open models we suggest 4-bit/8-bit profiles that maintain quality. we'll include quality regression checks as part of the pilot.
[02:45] Liam: cost tradeoff — we're sensitive to token spend. how do we decide Dedicated vs hosted?
[02:51] Samira: Dedicated gives predictable throughput and lower tail latency for high load and you get reserved GPU pools. Hosted is faster to start but cost per token can be higher in heavy usage. we can show cost estimates in the pricing sheet.
[03:04] Ava: and auditability? do dedicated deployments still provide the same audit logs?
[03:09] Jordan: yes, both Dedicated and Private options include audit logs; Private lets you push logs to your SIEM. Dedicated keeps data segregation but still through our control plane.
[03:18] Kevin: network — we'll need to know exact IP ranges for peering and egress allowed endpoints.
[03:23] Ethan: we'll provide a network diagram and CIDR ranges. for the bench we'll request temporary peering or a NAT range.
[03:31] [00:33] Jordan: rough pilot scope proposal — 6-week pilot: week 0 prep and network, week 1-2 integration and routing tests, week 3 full benchmark, week 4-5 quality evals and cost tuning, week 6 decision and rollout plan.
[03:49] Rosa: what about feature flags and rollouts? we want canary and rollback for models.
[03:54] Samira: Redwood supports route-level rollouts and canary policies; we can configure automatic fallback to smaller models when latency SLOs are missed.
[04:03] Maya: how intrusive is the SDK? we have a Python-based microservice ecosystem vs some Go services.
[04:09] Ethan: we have REST and SDKs for Python/Go/Node. SDK uses token-based auth; for enterprise we can map to SSO identities via SCIM.
[04:18] Liam: security again — KMS: do you require customer-managed keys for data or just for snapshots?
[04:24] Jordan: we can support CMK for model snapshots and at-rest storage for Private deployments; Hosted can optionally be configured to use your KMS depending on contract. we'll include specifics in the security packet.
[04:35] Ava: we need retention and delete workflows — right of erasure.
[04:38] Samira: we have retention policies and delete APIs; we'll document them and show how you can purge content on demand.
[04:46] Kevin: bench nuance — we have a mixture of short prompts (300 tokens) and long manifests (8-12k). need both measured. also offline reranking runs that are throughput-heavy but not latency-sensitive.
[04:58] Ethan: makes sense — we'll run two bench profiles: low-latency interactive and high-throughput batch rerank. recommend caching prefixes for the interactive path.
[05:08] Rosa: what's the expected engineering effort on our side?
[05:12] Jordan: initial integration typically 2-3 dev days to wire auth and basic API calls, then another week to wire up logging and SIEM. the bench sessions will require a few hours from your SRE to provision peering.
[05:25] Maya: we'd like an architecture sketch for how tokens flow and where we can scrub PII before sending.
[05:31] Ethan: we'll draw that up — show a pre-send redaction step in your app, then a proxy for token limiting, and then the call to Redwood with a cached KV layer.
[05:42] [05:43] Samira: question for Stonefield: what stakeholders need to be in the security review?
[05:47] Ava: me, our compliance lead (I'll loop in), and a product owner.
[05:50] Kevin: I'll also be on the call.
[05:52] Jordan: perfect. on pricing — we can model Hosted pilot costs and show Dedicated estimate for projected concurrency. we'll send a spreadsheet.
[06:01] Rosa: ok, governance — are there controls for prompt filtering or model whitelists?
[06:06] Jordan: yes, model catalog and route-level policy allow you to lock a route to a verified model id and disable others.
[06:13] Liam: question about fallback — if traffic spikes and model becomes unavailable, what's the rollback behavior?
[06:19] Ethan: we support automatic fallback to a pre-configured compatible model variant; we can also route to a lower-cost model if SLOs are missed.
[06:26] Ava: audit trail must show which model served the request and which user initiated it.
[06:30] Samira: that's in our audit logs surface — token-level attribution and model id included.
[06:34] Jordan: great. summary and tangible next steps: Jordan to send security pack and pricing by tomorrow; Ethan to prep bench harness and test plan; Maya to provision test VPC and share subnet info; Ava to send audit requirements. schedule bench for 11/18 at 10am PST if that works.
[06:51] Maya: 11/18 10am works.
[06:53] Kevin: works for me.
[06:55] Rosa: works.
[06:56] Jordan: ok, any last questions?
[06:59] Liam: just one — do you have a recommended model for manifest summarization?
[07:03] Ethan: we'll propose a shortlist (one higher-quality open model and one quantized faster variant) and include sample outputs so you can validate quality.
[07:12] Rosa: perfect.
[07:14] Jordan: thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the materials. meeting adjourned.
[07:18] [crosstalk] (recording stops)
questions: Can Redwood support KMS integration for hosted deployments?
What CIDR ranges are required for VPC peering?
Will Dedicated provide the same audit/logging surface as Private?
